sampling_model.design: Finite semi-Markovian structural causal model with observed-context whole-row CSI constraints; identification is population-level and introduces no sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: One population law on the fixed finite state space \(\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal X_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention is \(\operatorname{do}(X=\mathbf x)\), and the outcome cell is \(Y=\mathbf y\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive CPT entry is strictly positive as an explicit technical scope condition; each derived divisor also carries its own positivity judgment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of the identification kernel; a returned observed-cell functional passes to downstream estimation.

Theorem 5 proves termination and soundness of CSI search, while Theorem 6 shows that separate identification in every context graph is not complete.
Theorem 1 gives an if-and-only-if contextwise criterion for maximal-regular labels whose control variables are observed roots.
Theorem 1 proves soundness of a returned state-specific formula, and the paper does not claim general CSI completeness.
Theorem 1 characterizes classical positive-model identification through an invariant arithmetic-circuit cut found by the c-component method.
Theorem 1 states that the polynomial program gives sharp bounds for the encoded finite discrete causal problem.
The paper characterizes observational and interventional equivalence for fully observed context-specific staged-tree representations.

body.tldr: Fixed treatment and outcome assignments activate observed CSI information that variable-level identification can discard, but a local forest alone need not survive shared rows across contexts. The settled base case is a fixed-nuisance binary-sink certificate: the graph, row quotient, retained trace, and forest determine rational observed and query maps; row-space failure constructs a forest-supported kernel direction, and a single positive baseline plus an explicit radius yields two global shared-row models. The certificate stores neither model pair nor asserted observed or query comparisons. The field-tier kernel remains the open global context-factor dichotomy needed to extend this construction to coupled CPT blocks and obtain a complete arithmetic-formula-or-structural-obstruction procedure for observed endogenous activations.

project_justification.gap: Tikka et al. give sound CSI calculus and show that separate context graphs are incomplete. Mokhtarian et al. prove completeness for observed root controls, not observed endogenous activations. Chen and Darwiche give sound state-specific procedures without a complete obstruction theorem, and a local forest can be neutralized by cross-context row sharing.
project_justification.niche: Observed endogenous activation permits finite truth-table refinement while retaining shared CPT rows, reference-context recovery, cancellation, and information loss under active pruning.
project_justification.fill: The project first certifies the exact binary-sink lifting step through a forest-restricted row-space alternative and baseline perturbation, then asks whether provenance-carrying Q-factor recovery and partial traces force an analogous global multi-block dichotomy.

body.related_work: Boutilier et al. define local CSI through equality of conditional behavior, and Pensar et al. encode such equalities by labels; these works inform the canonical quotient. Shpitser and Pearl establish ordinary formula-or-hedge completeness, recovered when the CSI list is empty. Tikka et al., Theorems 5--6, prove sound CSI search and show that separate context-graph identification is insufficient; the proposed global dichotomy would add necessity. Mokhtarian et al., Theorem 1, prove an if-and-only-if criterion for maximal-regular labels activated by observed roots; roothood is essential to their conditioning reduction, so observed endogenous activations form a strict target domain rather than an attribution to that result. Chen and Darwiche, Theorem 1 and Proposition 5, supply a sound state-specific procedure and an active-pruning warning but no general completeness theorem. Their circuit work and Duarte et al.'s sharp polynomial programs inform finite algebraic contraction but do not provide a forest-derived shared-row kernel. Kivva et al. supply a positivity-aware generalized-identification comparator. Duarte and Solus characterize fully observed context-specific representations rather than latent query fibers. Bhattacharya et al. provide downstream estimation after a functional is returned, and the \(Y_0\) paper supplies the direct software consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A rooted C-forest is not by itself a nonidentification certificate under shared CSI rows. In the reference-context bow, the \(A=0\) cells place the query coefficient in the observed row space and force structural rejection. Maximal active deletion also fails: in the five-node rational pair, the pruned graph has no hedge although the empty trace carries a kernel direction with query gap \(3/200\). The global theorem must therefore retain partial traces and prove a forest-supported kernel statement after all cross-context contractions; generic real-algebraic fiber testing does not supply this linkage or total arithmetic descent.
body.honest_scope: The canonical quotient, SUCCESS soundness, fixed-nuisance binary-sink affine map, forest-to-kernel row-space alternative, baseline perturbation soundness theorem, finite structural bound, and two rational boundary fixtures are supporting results. The global context-factor dichotomy is visibly open and remains the completeness kernel. No general certificate-soundness or complete procedure is claimed before multi-block forest lifting is established. Strict primitive-CPT positivity and observed endogenous activation are transparent novel scope conditions. With no CSI, the syntax reduces to ordinary \(\mathrm{ID}\); on observed root activations, any complete answer must reproduce the published maximal-regular criterion. Estimation is downstream.
